finding.title: Route account_actions_sheet.dart's Sign Out / Delete Account icon glyphs through a theme token instead of a Colors.white literal
finding.rule: no_color_literal_outside_theme (custom_lint, currently broken/unenforced per novelty filter item 4)
finding.why: account_actions_sheet.dart's Sign Out and Delete Account icon glyphs are Colors.white literals, even though the rest of the same file consistently routes color through AppTheme.*/AppColors.*/theme.colorScheme.* (e.g. lines 128,140,152,160,178,188,204,261). an7_destructive_icon_contrast_test.dart pins this literal as the expected value rather than a themed constant, so the AN-7 contrast fix has no named, reusable 'high-contrast-on-errorContainer' token — a future theme edit (e.g. a dark-mode errorContainer swap) has no single place to update and could silently reintroduce an AN-7-class invisible-icon bug elsewhere that reuses the same pattern without the literal.
finding.recommendation: Add a named theme constant (e.g. an AppTheme.onErrorContainer-style token fixed to a contrasting value) and reference it at both call sites instead of the Colors.white literal; update an7_destructive_icon_contrast_test.dart to assert against that constant.
acceptance_criteria: account_actions_sheet.dart's two destructive-icon color values reference a named theme constant, not a Colors.white literal.
`dart run custom_lint` (once its analyzer-version crash is fixed) reports no no_color_literal_outside_theme violation for these two lines.

finding.title: Rewrite sign_out_dialog_l10n_test.dart to exercise the real showSignOutConfirmation, not a hand-copied dialog

evidence.quote: // Build the inner dialog widget directly (same builder used / inside showSignOutConfirmation) rather than calling the full

finding.why: All 4 tests in this file (verified green via `flutter test`) pump a Dialog the test author re-typed inline; the file never imports account_actions.dart, so it can never call the real showSignOutConfirmation. The copy even reads a different l10n getter for the title (l10n.signOut) than production uses (l10n.signOutConfirmTitle) — they coincide today only because both EN and HE ARB values happen to match. If a future edit to the real dialog (a HOTSPOT file, most-churned across fix waves) reintroduces a hardcoded string, breaks the reauth/sign-out flow, or diverges the title key, this suite stays green and the regression ships untested.
finding.recommendation: Either (a) extract the dialog's UI into a standalone widget (e.g. SignOutConfirmationDialog) that showSignOutConfirmation calls, and pump that widget directly in the test, or (b) build a full ProviderScope harness (router/registry/auth overrides) and call showSignOutConfirmation itself. Delete the inline duplicate.
acceptance_criteria: sign_out_dialog_l10n_test.dart imports and invokes the production showSignOutConfirmation (or a widget it delegates to) rather than a hand-copied Dialog.
Temporarily hardcoding an English string inside the real dialog builder makes this suite fail red; reverting makes it pass green.
Title text assertions resolve through the same AppLocalizations getter the production widget uses (signOutConfirmTitle), not a stand-in (signOut).

finding.title: Add the showDeleteLocalAccountFlow tests settings_utils_test.dart's docstring claims already exist

evidence.quote: //   A1. showDeleteLocalAccountFlow: non-localBorn auth state → exits immediately / //   A2. showDeleteLocalAccountFlow: localBorn → delete dialog shown

finding.why: Running the file (`flutter test settings_utils_test.dart`) shows exactly 11 tests (S1-S11); A1/A2 don't exist. `grep -rn showDeleteLocalAccountFlow test/` across the whole repo returns zero hits outside this docstring, and account_actions_test.dart (which the comment says 'does not cover' this) also has none. showDeleteLocalAccountFlow is the irreversible local-account-deletion path (closes the Drift handle, deletes the account DB file, clears the device-registry row and session) called from 3 lib sites including the HOTSPOT account_actions.dart; it ships with zero regression coverage while a comment implies it's covered.
finding.recommendation: Write A1 (non-localBorn auth state returns without showing any dialog) and A2 (localBorn auth state shows the delete-confirmation dialog and, once confirmed, drives the delete-local-account path) using the same DB/registry fakes account_management_service_test.dart already has, or delete the stale docstring lines if coverage is intentionally deferred and track it as a real ticket instead.
acceptance_criteria: test/features/settings/settings_utils_test.dart (or a relocated file, see AG-5 finding) contains passing A1 and A2 tests exercising showDeleteLocalAccountFlow directly.
grep -rn 'showDeleteLocalAccountFlow' test/ matches at least one real test body, not just a comment.

finding.title: Move PointConfigScreen and send_logs_service tests off the settings grab-bag files onto AG-5-mirrored paths
finding.why: PointConfigScreen lives in lib/features/gamification/presentation/screens/, not settings, yet its only widget-level coverage sits in a settings-tree file with no gamification counterpart; a developer looking under test/features/gamification/ for PointConfigScreen tests finds nothing. Meanwhile SettingsScreen — a HOTSPOT most-churned across fix waves — now has its coverage split across 3 unrelated files (this one, presentation/screens/settings_screen_test.dart, and settings_screen_r5_regression_test.dart) with no single mirrored source of truth. settings_utils_test.dart is a literal '_utils'-named grab-bag combining send_logs_service.dart coverage with an unfulfilled account_actions.dart supplement — the '_utils.dart god-file' pattern the naming rules explicitly forbid, applied to a test file.
finding.recommendation: Move the PointConfigScreen tests to test/features/gamification/presentation/screens/point_config_screen_test.dart. Move/merge the SettingsScreen tests into the existing test/features/settings/presentation/screens/settings_screen_test.dart. Rename settings_utils_test.dart's send_logs_service.dart coverage to test/features/settings/presentation/utils/send_logs_service_test.dart.
acceptance_criteria: test/features/gamification/presentation/screens/point_config_screen_test.dart exists and lib/features/gamification/presentation/screens/point_config_screen.dart's tests live only there.
SettingsScreen's widget-level tests are discoverable from a single mirrored path (or a cross-reference in settings_screen_test.dart) rather than 3 unrelated top-level files.
No file under test/ is named '<feature>_utils_test.dart' without a same-named lib file to mirror.

finding.title: Split the 3 settings test files that exceed the 400-line AG-3 limit (866/1255/573 lines)

evidence.quote: // L1 widget tests for SettingsScreen + PointConfigScreen

finding.why: `wc -l` gives 866 / 1255 / 573 lines respectively — 2.2x / 3.1x / 1.4x the 400-line hand-written-Dart ceiling. Files this large are slow to review end-to-end, hide unrelated concerns behind one main(), and make it easier for a reviewer to miss that a change touched an untested branch (as in the A1/A2 gap in the same file).
finding.recommendation: Split each file along its existing group() boundaries — e.g. backup_sync_section_l1_test.dart into a synced/syncing/pending file and a degraded/re-auth file; settings_screen_and_point_config_l1_test.dart per the AG-5 finding above; settings_utils_test.dart into send_logs_service_test.dart plus the (currently missing) account_actions supplement.
acceptance_criteria: `find test -name '*_test.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400{print}'` no longer lists any of these 3 paths.
A committed Rule-0 checker (e.g. a line-count script wired into `make audit`) fails CI on any hand-written .dart file over 400 lines, since no such checker exists today for AG-3.
